passages.text: Again the LORD spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho: “Command the Israelites to give, from the inheritance they will possess, cities for the Levites to live in and pasturelands around the cities.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
This happened on the plains of Moab.
The plains of Moab are by the Jordan River.
The Jordan River is across from Jericho.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to command the Israelites.
The Israelites will receive an inheritance in the land.
The LORD told the Israelites to give cities to the Levites.
The Levites are a tribe of Israel.
The Levites need cities to live in.
The Israelites must also give pasturelands to the Levites.
The pasturelands must be around the cities.
The cities and pasturelands come from the Israelites’ inheritance.
The Levites will live in these cities and use the pasturelands.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּעַֽרְבֹ֣ת מוֹאָ֑ב עַל־ יַרְדֵּ֥ן יְרֵח֖וֹ לֵאמֹֽר׃ צַו֮ אֶת־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וְנָתְנ֣וּ לַלְוִיִּ֗ם מִֽנַּחֲלַ֛ת אֲחֻזָּתָ֖ם עָרִ֣ים לָשָׁ֑בֶת וּמִגְרָ֗שׁ לֶֽעָרִים֙ סְבִיבֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם תִּתְּנ֖וּ לַלְוִיִּֽם׃

passages.text: The cities will be for them to live in, and the pasturelands will be for their herds, their flocks, and all their other livestock.
passages.sermon:
The Levites are a tribe of Israel.
God commanded the Israelites to give cities to the Levites.
The Levites will live in these cities.
The Israelites must also give pasturelands around these cities.
The Levites will use the pasturelands for their herds.
The Levites will use the pasturelands for their flocks.
The Levites will use the pasturelands for all their other livestock.
passages.original: וְהָי֧וּ הֶֽעָרִ֛ים לָהֶ֖ם לָשָׁ֑בֶת וּמִגְרְשֵׁיהֶ֗ם יִהְי֤וּ לִבְהֶמְתָּם֙ וְלִרְכֻשָׁ֔ם וּלְכֹ֖ל חַיָּתָֽם׃

passages.text: The pasturelands around the cities you are to give the Levites will extend a thousand cubits from the wall on every side.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave Moses instructions for the Israelites.
The Israelites must give cities to the Levites.
The Levites are a tribe set apart for service to God.
The Israelites must also give pasturelands around these cities to the Levites.
The pasturelands must extend outward from the city wall.
The distance must be one thousand cubits from the wall.
This distance must be measured on every side of the city.
passages.original: וּמִגְרְשֵׁי֙ הֶֽעָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּתְּנ֖וּ לַלְוִיִּ֑ם מִקִּ֤יר הָעִיר֙ וָח֔וּצָה אֶ֥לֶף אַמָּ֖ה סָבִֽיב׃

passages.text: You are also to measure two thousand cubits outside the city on the east, two thousand on the south, two thousand on the west, and two thousand on the north, with the city in the center. These areas will serve as larger pasturelands for the cities.
passages.sermon:
God gave instructions for the Levites.
The Levites are a tribe in Israel.
You must measure land outside each city.
Measure two thousand cubits to the east.
Measure two thousand cubits to the south.
Measure two thousand cubits to the west.
Measure two thousand cubits to the north.
The city must be in the center.
These measured areas will be pasturelands for the cities.
passages.original: וּמַדֹּתֶ֞ם מִח֣וּץ לָעִ֗יר אֶת־ פְּאַת־ קֵ֣דְמָה אַלְפַּ֪יִם בָּֽאַמָּ֟ה וְאֶת־ פְּאַת־ נֶגֶב֩ אַלְפַּ֨יִם בָּאַמָּ֜ה וְאֶת־ פְּאַת־ יָ֣ם׀ אַלְפַּ֣יִם בָּֽאַמָּ֗ה וְאֵ֨ת פְּאַ֥ת צָפ֛וֹן אַלְפַּ֥יִם בָּאַמָּ֖ה וְהָעִ֣יר בַּתָּ֑וֶךְ זֶ֚ה יִהְיֶ֣ה לָהֶ֔ם מִגְרְשֵׁ֖י הֶעָרִֽים׃

passages.text: Six of the cities you give the Levites are to be appointed as cities of refuge, to which a manslayer may flee. In addition to these, give the Levites forty-two other cities.
passages.sermon:
The Levites are a tribe in Israel.
You must give cities to the Levites.
Six of these cities must be cities of refuge.
A person who kills someone by accident may flee to a city of refuge.
You must also give the Levites forty-two more cities.
passages.original: וְאֵ֣ת הֶֽעָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר תִּתְּנוּ֙ לַלְוִיִּ֔ם אֵ֚ת שֵׁשׁ־ עָרֵ֣י הַמִּקְלָ֔ט אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּתְּנ֔וּ לָנֻ֥ס שָׁ֖מָּה הָרֹצֵ֑חַ וַעֲלֵיהֶ֣ם תִּתְּנ֔וּ אַרְבָּעִ֥ים וּשְׁתַּ֖יִם עִֽיר׃

passages.text: The total number of cities you give the Levites will be forty-eight, with their corresponding pasturelands.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave instructions to the Israelites.
The Israelites must give cities to the Levites.
The total number of these cities must be forty-eight.
Each city must have its own pastureland.
passages.original: כָּל־ הֶעָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר תִּתְּנוּ֙ לַלְוִיִּ֔ם אַרְבָּעִ֥ים וּשְׁמֹנֶ֖ה עִ֑יר אֶתְהֶ֖ן וְאֶת־ מִגְרְשֵׁיהֶֽן׃

passages.text: The cities that you apportion from the territory of the Israelites should be given to the Levites in proportion to the inheritance of each tribe: more from a larger tribe and less from a smaller one.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave instructions to the Israelites.
The Israelites must give cities to the Levites.
These cities come from the land each tribe receives.
Each tribe must give cities in proportion to its inheritance.
A larger tribe must give more cities.
A smaller tribe must give fewer cities.
Each person must give from his own cities to the Levites.
passages.original: וְהֶֽעָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר תִּתְּנוּ֙ מֵאֲחֻזַּ֣ת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מֵאֵ֤ת הָרַב֙ תַּרְבּ֔וּ וּמֵאֵ֥ת הַמְעַ֖ט תַּמְעִ֑יטוּ אִ֗ישׁ כְּפִ֤י נַחֲלָתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִנְחָ֔לוּ יִתֵּ֥ן מֵעָרָ֖יו לַלְוִיִּֽם׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan, designate cities to serve as your cities of refuge, so that a person who kills someone unintentionally may flee there.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to speak to the Israelites.
The LORD said, "You will cross the Jordan River."
You will enter the land of Canaan.
You must choose cities for yourselves.
These cities will be cities of refuge for you.
A person who kills someone by accident may flee to these cities.
These cities will protect the person who killed unintentionally.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם כִּ֥י אַתֶּ֛ם עֹבְרִ֥ים אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן אַ֥רְצָה כְּנָֽעַן׃ וְהִקְרִיתֶ֤ם לָכֶם֙ עָרִ֔ים עָרֵ֥י מִקְלָ֖ט תִּהְיֶ֣ינָה לָכֶ֑ם וְנָ֥ס שָׁ֙מָּה֙ רֹצֵ֔חַ מַכֵּה־ נֶ֖פֶשׁ בִּשְׁגָגָֽה׃

passages.text: You are to have these cities as a refuge from the avenger, so that the manslayer will not die until he stands trial before the assembly.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave instructions to the Israelites.
God told them to set aside cities of refuge.
These cities will protect people who kill someone unintentionally.
These cities will keep the killer safe from the avenger.
The killer will not die before standing trial.
The assembly will judge the case.
passages.original: וְהָי֨וּ לָכֶ֧ם הֶעָרִ֛ים לְמִקְלָ֖ט מִגֹּאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֤א יָמוּת֙ הָרֹצֵ֔חַ עַד־ עָמְד֛וֹ לִפְנֵ֥י הָעֵדָ֖ה לַמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: The cities you select will be your six cities of refuge.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave instructions to the Israelites.
God told them to choose cities.
You must select six cities.
These six cities will be your cities of refuge.
passages.original: וְהֶעָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּתֵּ֑נוּ שֵׁשׁ־ עָרֵ֥י מִקְלָ֖ט תִּהְיֶ֥ינָה לָכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Select three cities across the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan as cities of refuge.
passages.sermon:
God commanded the Israelites to set apart cities of refuge.
They must choose six cities in total.
They must select three cities across the Jordan River.
They must select three cities in the land of Canaan.
These six cities will serve as cities of refuge.
passages.original: אֵ֣ת׀ שְׁלֹ֣שׁ הֶעָרִ֗ים תִּתְּנוּ֙ מֵעֵ֣בֶר לַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וְאֵת֙ שְׁלֹ֣שׁ הֶֽעָרִ֔ים תִּתְּנ֖וּ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן עָרֵ֥י מִקְלָ֖ט תִּהְיֶֽינָה׃

passages.text: These six cities will serve as a refuge for the Israelites and for the foreigner or stranger among them, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.
passages.sermon:
God commanded the Israelites to set aside six cities.
These cities are called cities of refuge.
The six cities are for the Israelites.
The six cities are also for foreigners living among them.
The six cities are also for strangers living among them.
Anyone who kills a person by accident may flee to these cities.
These cities will protect those who killed unintentionally.
passages.original: לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְלַגֵּ֤ר וְלַתּוֹשָׁב֙ בְּתוֹכָ֔ם תִּהְיֶ֛ינָה שֵׁשׁ־ הֶעָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לְמִקְלָ֑ט לָנ֣וּס שָׁ֔מָּה כָּל־ מַכֵּה־ נֶ֖פֶשׁ בִּשְׁגָגָֽה׃

passages.text: If, however, anyone strikes a person with an iron object and kills him, he is a murderer; the murderer must surely be put to death.
passages.sermon: A person may strike another person with an iron object.\r\nIf the person who is struck dies, the one who struck him is a murderer.\r\nThe murderer must be put to death.
passages.original: וְאִם־ בִּכְלִ֨י בַרְזֶ֧ל׀ הִכָּ֛הוּ וַיָּמֹ֖ת רֹצֵ֣חַֽ ה֑וּא מ֥וֹת יוּמַ֖ת הָרֹצֵֽחַ׃

passages.text: Or if anyone has in his hand a stone of deadly size, and he strikes and kills another, he is a murderer; the murderer must surely be put to death.
passages.sermon:
This law is for the Israelites and for any foreigner or stranger living among them.
God gave six cities as places of refuge.
Anyone who kills a person by accident may run to these cities for safety.
If a person holds a stone that can kill someone, and he strikes another person with it, and that person dies, then the one who struck is a murderer.
The murderer must be put to death.
passages.original: וְאִ֡ם בְּאֶ֣בֶן יָד֩ אֲשֶׁר־ יָמ֨וּת בָּ֥הּ הִכָּ֛הוּ וַיָּמֹ֖ת רֹצֵ֣חַֽ ה֑וּא מ֥וֹת יוּמַ֖ת הָרֹצֵֽחַ׃

passages.text: If anyone has in his hand a deadly object of wood, and he strikes and kills another, he is a murderer; the murderer must surely be put to death.
passages.sermon:
A person may hold a wooden object in his hand.
This wooden object can kill someone.
If the person strikes another with this object and the other person dies, he is a murderer.
The murderer must be put to death.
passages.original: א֡וֹ בִּכְלִ֣י עֵֽץ־ יָד֩ אֲשֶׁר־ יָמ֨וּת בּ֥וֹ הִכָּ֛הוּ וַיָּמֹ֖ת רֹצֵ֣חַֽ ה֑וּא מ֥וֹת יוּמַ֖ת הָרֹצֵֽחַ׃

passages.text: The avenger of blood is to put the murderer to death; when he finds him, he is to kill him.
passages.sermon: The avenger of blood is a close relative of the person who was killed.\r\nThe avenger of blood must put the murderer to death.\r\nWhen the avenger of blood finds the murderer, he must kill him.
passages.original: גֹּאֵ֣ל הַדָּ֔ם ה֥וּא יָמִ֖ית אֶת־ הָרֹצֵ֑חַ בְּפִגְעוֹ־ ב֖וֹ ה֥וּא יְמִיתֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Likewise, if anyone maliciously pushes another or intentionally throws an object at him and kills him, or if in hostility he strikes him with his hand and he dies, the one who struck him must surely be put to death; he is a murderer. When the avenger of blood finds the murderer, he is to kill him.
passages.sermon:
If a person acts with hatred, he pushes another person.
Or he throws an object at another person on purpose.
If the other person dies, the one who acted is guilty.
If a person strikes another with his hand in hostility, and the other dies, the striker is guilty.
The one who killed is a murderer.
The murderer must be put to death.
The avenger of blood will kill the murderer when he finds him.
passages.original: וְאִם־ בְּשִׂנְאָ֖ה יֶהְדָּפֶ֑נּוּ אֽוֹ־ הִשְׁלִ֥יךְ עָלָ֛יו בִּצְדִיָּ֖ה וַיָּמֹֽת׃ א֣וֹ בְאֵיבָ֞ה הִכָּ֤הוּ בְיָדוֹ֙ וַיָּמֹ֔ת מֽוֹת־ יוּמַ֥ת הַמַּכֶּ֖ה רֹצֵ֣חַֽ ה֑וּא גֹּאֵ֣ל הַדָּ֗ם יָמִ֛ית אֶת־ הָרֹצֵ֖חַ בְּפִגְעוֹ־ בֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But if anyone pushes a person suddenly, without hostility, or throws an object at him unintentionally, or without looking drops a heavy stone that kills him, but he was not an enemy and did not intend to harm him, then the congregation must judge between the slayer and the avenger of blood according to these ordinances.
passages.sermon:
A person may push another person suddenly.
He may do this without hostility.
He may throw an object at someone without meaning to harm him.
He may drop a heavy stone without seeing the other person.
The stone may fall on the person and kill him.
The one who caused the death was not an enemy.
He did not intend to harm the other person.
The congregation must judge this case.
They must judge between the one who struck and the avenger of blood.
They must use these ordinances to make their judgment.
passages.original: וְאִם־ בְּפֶ֥תַע בְּלֹא־ אֵיבָ֖ה הֲדָפ֑וֹ אוֹ־ הִשְׁלִ֥יךְ עָלָ֛יו כָּל־ כְּלִ֖י בְּלֹ֥א צְדִיָּֽה׃ א֣וֹ בְכָל־ אֶ֜בֶן אֲשֶׁר־ יָמ֥וּת בָּהּ֙ בְּלֹ֣א רְא֔וֹת וַיַּפֵּ֥ל עָלָ֖יו וַיָּמֹ֑ת וְהוּא֙ לֹא־ אוֹיֵ֣ב ל֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א מְבַקֵּ֖שׁ רָעָתֽוֹ׃ וְשָֽׁפְטוּ֙ הָֽעֵדָ֔ה בֵּ֚ין הַמַּכֶּ֔ה וּבֵ֖ין גֹּאֵ֣ל הַדָּ֑ם עַ֥ל הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

passages.text: The assembly is to protect the manslayer from the hand of the avenger of blood. Then the assembly will return him to the city of refuge to which he fled, and he must live there until the death of the high priest, who was anointed with the holy oil.
passages.sermon:
The assembly must protect the manslayer.
The manslayer killed someone without intent or hatred.
The avenger of blood wants to kill the manslayer.
The assembly must save the manslayer from the avenger of blood.
The assembly must return the manslayer to his city of refuge.
The manslayer fled to this city for safety.
The manslayer must stay in the city of refuge.
He must remain there until the high priest dies.
The high priest was anointed with holy oil.
passages.original: וְהִצִּ֨ילוּ הָעֵדָ֜ה אֶת־ הָרֹצֵ֗חַ מִיַּד֮ גֹּאֵ֣ל הַדָּם֒ וְהֵשִׁ֤יבוּ אֹתוֹ֙ הָֽעֵדָ֔ה אֶל־ עִ֥יר מִקְלָט֖וֹ אֲשֶׁר־ נָ֣ס שָׁ֑מָּה וְיָ֣שַׁב בָּ֗הּ עַד־ מוֹת֙ הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּדֹ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־ מָשַׁ֥ח אֹת֖וֹ בְּשֶׁ֥מֶן הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃

passages.text: But if the manslayer ever goes outside the limits of the city of refuge to which he fled and the avenger of blood finds him outside of his city of refuge and kills him, then the avenger will not be guilty of bloodshed because the manslayer must remain in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest. Only after the death of the high priest may he return to the land he owns.
passages.sermon:
A manslayer is someone who killed another person accidentally.
The manslayer fled to a city of refuge.
The city of refuge is a safe place for the manslayer.
If the manslayer leaves the city of refuge,
He goes outside its boundaries.
If the avenger of blood finds the manslayer outside the city of refuge,
The avenger of blood may kill the manslayer.
The avenger of blood is not guilty for killing the manslayer outside the city of refuge.
The manslayer must stay in the city of refuge.
He must remain there until the high priest dies.
After the high priest dies,
The manslayer may return to his own land.
passages.original: וְאִם־ יָצֹ֥א יֵצֵ֖א הָרֹצֵ֑חַ אֶת־ גְּבוּל֙ עִ֣יר מִקְלָט֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָנ֖וּס שָֽׁמָּה׃ וּמָצָ֤א אֹתוֹ֙ גֹּאֵ֣ל הַדָּ֔ם מִח֕וּץ לִגְב֖וּל עִ֣יר מִקְלָט֑וֹ וְרָצַ֞ח גֹּאֵ֤ל הַדָּם֙ אֶת־ הָ֣רֹצֵ֔חַ אֵ֥ין ל֖וֹ דָּֽם׃ כִּ֣י בְעִ֤יר מִקְלָטוֹ֙ יֵשֵׁ֔ב עַד־ מ֖וֹת הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּדֹ֑ל וְאַחֲרֵ֥י מוֹת֙ הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּדֹ֔ל יָשׁוּב֙ הָרֹצֵ֔חַ אֶל־ אֶ֖רֶץ אֲחֻזָּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: This will be a statutory ordinance for you for the generations to come, wherever you live.
passages.sermon:
God gave these laws to Israel.
These laws are permanent.
These laws are for all your generations.
These laws apply wherever you live.
passages.original: וְהָי֨וּ אֵ֧לֶּה לָכֶ֛ם לְחֻקַּ֥ת מִשְׁפָּ֖ט לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶ֑ם בְּכֹ֖ל מוֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: If anyone kills a person, the murderer is to be put to death on the testimony of the witnesses. But no one is to be put to death based on the testimony of a lone witness.
passages.sermon:
A person who kills another person is called a murderer.
The community must put the murderer to death.
They must do this only if there are witnesses.
There must be more than one witness.
If only one person testifies, do not put the murderer to death.
passages.original: כָּל־ מַ֨כֵּה־ נֶ֔פֶשׁ לְפִ֣י עֵדִ֔ים יִרְצַ֖ח אֶת־ הָרֹצֵ֑חַ וְעֵ֣ד אֶחָ֔ד לֹא־ יַעֲנֶ֥ה בְנֶ֖פֶשׁ לָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: You are not to accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who deserves to die; he must surely be put to death.
passages.sermon:
God gave a law to the Israelites.
This law applies to all their generations.
This law applies wherever they live.
A murderer is someone who kills another person and is guilty of death.
You must not accept money or any ransom for the life of a murderer.
A murderer who deserves to die must be put to death.
You must not let a murderer escape punishment by paying a ransom.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ תִקְח֥וּ כֹ֙פֶר֙ לְנֶ֣פֶשׁ רֹצֵ֔חַ אֲשֶׁר־ ה֥וּא רָשָׁ֖ע לָמ֑וּת כִּי־ מ֖וֹת יוּמָֽת׃

passages.text: Nor should you accept a ransom for the person who flees to a city of refuge and allow him to return and live on his own land before the death of the high priest.
passages.sermon:
God gave laws to Israel about justice and the land.
A person may kill someone and flee to a city of refuge.
This person seeks safety in the city of refuge.
You must not accept money from this person.
You must not let him pay a ransom to return to his own land.
He must stay in the city of refuge.
He cannot return home before the high priest dies.
passages.original: וְלֹא־ תִקְח֣וּ כֹ֔פֶר לָנ֖וּס אֶל־ עִ֣יר מִקְלָט֑וֹ לָשׁוּב֙ לָשֶׁ֣בֶת בָּאָ֔רֶץ עַד־ מ֖וֹת הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

passages.text: Do not pollute the land where you live, for bloodshed pollutes the land, and no atonement can be made for the land on which the blood is shed, except by the blood of the one who shed it.
passages.sermon:
You live in this land.
Do not pollute the land.
Bloodshed pollutes the land.
If someone sheds blood in the land, the land becomes polluted.
No atonement can be made for the land where blood was shed.
Only the blood of the one who shed it can atone for the land.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ תַחֲנִ֣יפוּ אֶת־ הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתֶּם֙ בָּ֔הּ כִּ֣י הַדָּ֔ם ה֥וּא יַחֲנִ֖יף אֶת־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וְלָאָ֣רֶץ לֹֽא־ יְכֻפַּ֗ר לַדָּם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שֻׁפַּךְ־ בָּ֔הּ כִּי־ אִ֖ם בְּדַ֥ם שֹׁפְכֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Do not defile the land where you live and where I dwell. For I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites.”
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God dwells among the Israelites.
You live in the land.
God also dwells in this land.
Do not defile the land.
passages.original: וְלֹ֧א תְטַמֵּ֣א אֶת־ הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתֶּם֙ יֹשְׁבִ֣ים בָּ֔הּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י שֹׁכֵ֣ן בְּתוֹכָ֑הּ כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה שֹׁכֵ֕ן בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
